edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a harmful direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: children followed into adolescence or adulthood
edges.mechanism: Lead interferes with synapse development and calcium-dependent neuronal signaling during a period when the brain is especially plastic, helping explain durable cognitive losses.
edges.summary: The strongest piece here is the 2023 Halabicky cohort in J Expo Sci Environ Epidemiol, which ties childhood lead exposure to cognitive function in a direction that later studies largely support. That makes this edge more about calibrating magnitude and context than arguing over whether the signal exists at all.
edges.caveats: Residual confounding and reverse causation remain possible in some observational studies, so the main readout is direction and plausibility rather than one exact risk number.
